findings.title: Cache lock no longer prevents concurrent index builds for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex now only locks cacheMu when inserting into b.cache. It does not prevent two goroutines from building the same NamespacedResource concurrently. searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex can call BuildIndex concurrently for a missing index (search requests plus the watch event handler). Concurrent builds can create duplicate indexes, overwrite the cache entry, lose watch writes already applied to the replaced index, and for file-backed indexes may contend on the same directory. A per-key lock/singleflight or check-for-existing under lock is needed.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads the index cache without locking
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex can write to the map concurrently (now only briefly locked). Concurrent map iteration and write can race and panic. It should take cacheMu.RLock before iterating.

findings.title: errgroup workers share outer err and increment counter without synchronization
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup worker assigns to the outer err variable from GetResourceStats and increments totalBatchesIndexed without atomics or a mutex. Because group.Go runs concurrently, this is a data race; the span count is unreliable and a worker can return an error value that another goroutine overwrote. Use a local err inside the closure and an atomic counter or mutex for totalBatchesIndexed.

findings.title: Initial index build discards the resource version, allowing missed events
findings.body: searchSupport.build returns the resource version it indexed up to, but init discards that value and only after all builds calls storage.WatchWriteEvents, which starts from the backend's current latest version. Events written between the initial list/build and starting the watch are not replayed into the index, so the search index can remain stale. Start watching before backfilling or pass/use the returned resource version.

findings.title: Search watch loop does not handle channel closure and cannot be canceled
findings.body: The watch goroutine started in searchSupport.init reads from events without checking whether the channel is closed and uses context.Background. If the backend closes the watch channel (for example during Stop), the receive returns nil repeatedly and handleEvent will dereference a nil event, causing a panic or busy loop; the goroutine also cannot be canceled by ResourceServer.Stop. Use the server context and a comma-ok/select loop.

findings.title: History and Origin dereference s.search without nil check
findings.body: When search is not configured, s.search is nil. Search guards for nil, but History and Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin directly, causing a nil pointer panic if those gRPC methods are invoked. Add nil checks or return a clear configuration error.

findings.title: initWatcher event-forwarding loop does not handle channel closure
findings.body: The event-forwarding goroutine in initWatcher reads from the backend watch channel without checking ok. If the backend closes the channel, v is nil and the next log/metric access dereferences v, causing a panic during shutdown or backend failure. It should handle channel closure and context cancellation.

findings.title: Init failure leaks context cancel and lifecycle resources
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancellable context and may run lifecycle.Init before calling s.Init. If s.Init fails, the constructor returns without calling cancel or stopping lifecycle hooks, leaking the context and any resources started during initialization. Cleanup should be performed on failure.
